money_at_stake.rationale: Two separately-dated pools sit inside this occurrence's window and are additive rather than alternative, so this is deliberately not one point estimate. Pool one is already in force: the original Section 338 action (signed 2026-07-20, effective 2026-08-22 per the occurrence's own dated claim) covers nearly USD 20bn of Canadian imports across motor vehicles, alcohol and dairy, per USTR's own release, fetched directly this run; USD 20bn alone already sits inside B10_100 (USD 10bn to 100bn), not merely B1_10 as an earlier draft of this rationale imprecisely stated. Pool two is the escalation Nell's card centers on: on 2026-08-24 the President stated via a Truth Social post that Section 338 tariffs on Canadian cars, trucks, automotive parts and steel rise to 50 percent effective 2027-01-01. The trade this touches is not small: US 2025 imports of Canadian passenger cars (USD 25.27bn), goods vehicles (USD 5.65bn) and parts and accessories (USD 11.01bn), per UN Comtrade as reported by a secondary analysis fetched this run, sum to roughly USD 41.9bn, itself independently inside B10_100. Both pools individually clear B10_100 and, summed, would total roughly USD 62bn, still short of GT_100B. Not summed into one headline figure because the two actions have different legal triggers, different in-force dates and are reported from different data vintages, the same discipline the standing LEAKY appraisal applied to three non-comparable Arctic programs.

public_reach.rationale: Every named party on both sides of the auto-tariff dispute confirmed this run is a listed issuer: Ford, Stellantis and General Motors are all NYSE-listed OEMs with direct Canadian assembly exposure, and the market repriced them the same day the escalation was announced. This is still the opposite of the standing LEAKY case: a dispute between two G7 governments conducted through public companies, with no sanctioned or state-owned enterprise anywhere in the auto side of the chain. Scored down from a prior 88 because the second half of the original reach argument, that protected domestic steel producers (Cleveland-Cliffs, Nucor) also repriced the same day, rested on a source (Invezz) that returned HTTP 403 on refetch this run with no reachable archive copy, and has been removed rather than repaired with a substitute source. What remains cited is the auto and assembly side alone: still a majority-listed, majority-public dispute, but this run does not independently confirm the steel side's public-market reach, the Canadian tier-2/3 parts base's listing status, or which specific Canadian retaliation targets are themselves publicly traded.

capture_odds.rationale: Confirmed this run only on the cost side: cross-border-integrated automakers (Ford, Stellantis, GM) fell the day the escalation was announced, meaning the tariff reads to the market as a margin cost they absorb rather than a pool they capture. The dollar-weighted majority of the occurrence, the roughly USD 42bn of cross-border auto and parts trade, sits on this confirmed cost side. The prior run's other half of the bifurcation argument, that protected domestic steel producers (Cleveland-Cliffs, Nucor) capture pricing power and rose sharply the same day, rested on the same Invezz source that could not be refetched this run (HTTP 403, no reachable archive) and has been removed rather than repaired. Scored below the prior run's 42 because removing that citation removes the only evidenced capture-side mechanism in this appraisal: what remains cited supports cost-absorption on the larger side of the pool, with no currently-cited evidence of profit capture anywhere in the chain.

timing_fit.rationale: Money is already moving inside the window rather than merely projected into it: the USD 20bn initial wave has been collected since 2026-08-22 per the occurrence's own dated claim, and USTR's release confirms the thirty-day effective clock from the 2026-07-20 announcement; equities on both sides of the trade already repriced on 2026-08-24 (public_reach evidence). The larger escalation (cars, trucks, parts and steel to 50 percent) is dated 2027-01-01 per the occurrence record, comfortably inside the 2 to 5 year horizon and in fact near its front edge. Not scored above 75 (down from a prior 82) because, as of the most recent evidence fetched this run (2026-08-26), that escalation had been communicated only via a Truth Social post rather than a signed proclamation, and whether it removes the USMCA rules-of-origin exemption that currently lets self-certified parts enter free under HTS 9903.94.06 is reported as explicitly unresolved by Barclays' own read, meaning a real share of the announced dollar figure could still move on different terms before the date arrives. The prior run's additional corroboration, Canada's retaliation list value and its effective date, rested on a Tech Times source that returned HTTP 403 on refetch this run with no reachable archive, and has been removed rather than repaired; the occurrence record itself still places Canadian countermeasures starting 2026-09-08, but this run does not independently cite a dollar figure for that leg of the dispute.

notes.text: Independent verification note: Nell's card frames the January 2027 escalation as applying 'regardless of USMCA qualification, removing the rules-of-origin exemption that had protected parts' as settled fact. This run's research found that framing gets ahead of the record: as of the most recent dated source found (2026-08-26), the escalation exists only as a presidential social media statement with no signed proclamation, and a secondary analysis explicitly says whether the USMCA parts carve-out survives is unresolved ('Nobody knows... only a Truth Social post'). The already-in-force USD 20bn Section 338 wave (effective 2026-08-22, covering motor vehicles, alcohol and dairy) is confirmed against a primary USTR source and genuinely does apply regardless of USMCA per the statute's design, but that is the smaller of the two pools, not the one the card's narrative centers on. This does not change the band (money_at_stake still clears B10_100 on either pool alone) but it is why timing_fit is not scored higher: a real share of the headline dollar figure could still move on different terms before 2027-01-01.
